reviewsPage.summary: The reviews here split. One reviewer reports losing more than 30 pounds on the program, keeping it off, and having more energy since. Another names Nurse Alex as patient and thorough with questions throughout the process. The third describes paying thousands for blood work and supplements, waiting weeks for part of the order, and getting no reply from their wellness advisor until they booked a call themselves.

Both reviews are positive. One reviewer came in with chronic severe fatigue alongside other issues, says Dr. Hayes identified the cause quickly, and reports feeling significantly better and more energetic within a few weeks of starting treatment. Zach and the wider team are named. The second reviewer has used the practice since it operated as Tampa Rejuvenation and describes consistent communication from the front desk through the rest of the staff.

Two of the three reviewers name the team: Alex the surgical coordinator, Stephanie at the front desk, and Dr. Wiegers and Dr. Lustig for the procedures themselves, with one noting the options were laid out without a push to buy. The third came for PRP on hip injuries, paid a $1,000 consultation fee, and went elsewhere after the treatment appointment was rescheduled three times at short notice.

Reviews here are divided and all concern hormone pellet therapy. One reviewer, treated after having her ovaries removed, reports her hair stopped falling out and her sleep, mood and focus improved. The other two describe problems: complications after a first round of pellets and an explanation from the company they found unconvincing, and a menopause patient who says she was given a high testosterone dose alongside estrogen and progesterone, developed voice changes, extra body hair and bleeding, and felt dismissed when she raised it.

Both reviewers are long-term patients, one for more than 25 years and one for close to 30. They describe treatment for chronic pain conditions including Ehlers-Danlos syndrome and fibromyalgia, and credit Dr. Blatman with protocols that sit outside standard care. Jennifer and Lois are named alongside him. One reviewer says the care gave them their life back.

Two reviewers describe the appointment itself: Dr. Crane going through prior X-rays and MRI images in the room before recommending next steps, and Dr. Bayes treating a 17-year-old's UCL injury with a PRP injection across two unhurried visits. The third reviewer says they spent $6,000, gave the practice months of chances to resolve their complaint, and would send others elsewhere.

Two reviewers name Dr. Glowney, Dr. Rudolf and staff members Ryan and Dawn, and both emphasise the same thing: careful explanation and being told what to expect rather than being sold an outcome. The third was treated for long COVID headache and gastrointestinal symptoms, reports no benefit from a procedure they found painful and expensive, and says two other people they know had the same result.

Both reviews describe stem cell therapy for pain at the Las Vegas clinic, and both focus on the consultation: the process explained clearly, questions answered without being rushed, and a plan built around the individual rather than one protocol for everyone. Neither reviewer reports on results months later.

Three five-star reviews covering two services. One reviewer, who had two surgeries on the same shoulder and constant aching afterwards, says a single EPAT session cleared the discomfort and credits Mike for the assessment beforehand. The other two describe first-time colon hydrotherapy sessions with Carol and Monica, both noting they were talked through each step.

All three reviewers travelled from overseas. Two raise the same worry about a language barrier and say English-speaking staff and an English-fluent lead doctor settled it. The treatments described are aesthetic rather than orthopedic: one reviewer had Radiesse, a collagen-stimulating injectable, for smile lines, and calls the change subtle rather than dramatic. Each review mentions an assessment before anything was started.

Both reviewers describe the initial evaluation rather than any treatment that followed. One calls it the most thorough medical exam they have had and names Dr. Patel. The other met Dr. Leake, had blood drawn at home for convenience, and came away with preventive health information they valued. Both reviews are older, from two and six years ago.

Three five-star reviews. One covers a knee osteoarthritis case treated with regenerative orthopedics. Another describes the day of the procedure: Dr. Markle answering questions beforehand, staff support during it, and a call the next day to check on recovery. The third is about how the clinic runs, including Dr. Centeno's weekly public question session.

Two reviewers describe Chaum as a high-end check-up and anti-aging center where the doctor comes to the patient rather than the other way round, and both rate the program and facilities highly. The third came for a facial and other treatments, found the care acceptable, but says foreign patients are charged more and that they found comparable treatment elsewhere for less.

Both reviewers were treated by Dr. Harry Adelson. One had severe right knee pain and plantar fasciitis in the left foot after months of physical therapy that had not helped, and praises the care and the follow-up rather than describing a specific result. The other describes the atmosphere as calm and notes staff checking in while they recovered from a procedure.

The reviews cover hormone balancing, skin treatment and the practice itself. Two name their provider, Nicole Taylor and Katelyn, the latter for a first microneedling session. The third credits Samantha with helping balance her hormones and manage weight gain in her fifties, and still rates the clinic three stars because of what she calculates as a 50 to 60 percent markup on prescriptions over the outsourced pharmacy price.

All three reviews are about stem cell banking rather than treatment, and all are around five years old. Two reviewers describe the collection and storage process as straightforward and the ongoing updates as the reason they are glad they banked. The third pays $250 a year, says they have had no updates on research progress, and questions what the annual fee buys.

Two reviewers describe diagnostics rather than treatment: a five-hour Apex assessment that one says picked up problems which would have become serious if left, and a contrast study of the heart under Dr. Kingsbury. The third recommends against the clinic, citing the margin taken on prescribed supplements compared with other practitioners, and long waits.

Two international patients describe knee treatment. One had stem cell cartilage regeneration alongside a leg realignment procedure more than a year ago and returned to have the plate and screws removed while rebuilding athletic mobility. The other travelled to Seoul for a knee treatment using umbilical cord blood stem cells and rates the intensive rehabilitation program above the procedure itself. A third reviewer describes a consultation in which the doctor raised his voice and says patients were not treated with dignity.

Both reviewers rate the clinic five stars and both are specific about outcome. One was treated for extensive scar tissue and skin damage following radiation for breast cancer, and reports some skin improvement, scar tissue in the chest releasing, and more movement in the arm and chest wall. The other, who has severe emphysema and has had part of a lung removed, had noticed no change two months after the procedure and rates the clinic on how Dr. Johnson and the staff handled it.

These reviews are about supply and service rather than clinical care. Two name staff, Brooklyn and Rosa, for chasing a delayed order that needed refrigeration and for answering quickly. The third says shipments started arriving close to expiry and that compensation requests were passed to management and then to the pharmacy without a fast answer.

The reviews concern a remote prescription service. One reviewer went from 178 pounds to 140 over roughly a year and is now around 145 with more muscle. Another reports feeling better, with a thorough doctor and quick shipping. The third cancelled after a refill questionnaire went unreviewed for a week while they had two days of medication left.

Both reviews are five stars. One reviewer had six years of debilitating cervical instability from C1 through C7, was recommended PRP by Dr. Santa Ana, describes the first treatment as the turning point, and has since had a second. The other credits Dr. Nabity with taking time over conditions and options, and with trying to avoid surgery where he can.

All three reviewers are international patients treated for back or joint pain, and all describe the same pattern: imaging, consultation and treatment compressed into three or four hours, with an interpreter or English-speaking guide staying with them throughout. One names the translator, Jenny. The four-star review makes a single criticism, that the order of tests meant going through an MRI and X-ray twice after seeing different physicians.

Both reviews describe walk-in wellness services rather than regenerative treatment: a vitamin B injection and IV therapy, with Dani named for making the session comfortable. One reviewer was shown round the Sunset Plaza location and lists the infrared and oxygen equipment on offer. Both report feeling better the same day, and neither describes a longer course of treatment.

Two reviewers travelled to Seoul for regenerative treatment of long-standing pain, one for lower back pain specifically. Both name Dr. Kim and the physiotherapy staff, say they were given time to decide rather than pushed, and one has returned for further treatment with the same result. The third, also an international patient, says the bill came in well above the verbal quote, that they had under two minutes with the doctor, and that the English-speaking coordinator pressed surgical options they had not asked about.

The reviews are about hormone pellet therapy. Two long-term patients, one on testosterone and thyroid treatment for over ten years and one receiving pellets quarterly, report more energy and improvements in anxiety, low mood and focus, and the second names Rachel for checking levels and adjusting between visits. A third, a pellet patient since May 2024, says the clinic declined a scheduled testosterone pellet in January 2026 after they began hormone therapy through another provider.

Both reviewers rate PUR-FORM five stars and both write about the practice rather than a procedure: appointments that are easy to get, a responsive team, and nurses who check in during the visit. Nina and Gabi are named in one review. Neither review states which treatment was received or reports a clinical outcome.

Both reviewers describe a wellness plan built around them rather than a single procedure, and both name the staff who ran it: Savannah and Nicole in one case, Abby in the other. One says the team identified and addressed health and lifestyle problems that had been affecting them for years. Neither review covers a regenerative procedure.

Both reviews are five stars. One reviewer had a single injection into the shoulder and reports full recovery of range of motion alongside strength work afterwards. The other names Dr. Greene and Samantha, and describes a stem cell treatment plan explained in full and adapted to their case, with support at each stage.

One reviewer, treated for a meniscus tear in one knee and arthritis in the other following a 1996 ACL tear, says both knees felt good a week after the injections and that they were touring Panama two days later. A second names Dr. Ponte and describes the information given beforehand and the accommodation. The third had both shoulders treated, reports no improvement months on, says the shoulder that was fine has since worsened, and describes the aftercare as absent.

The available patient review describes treatment for an 11-year-old who was severely disabled after taking fluoroquinolone antibiotics. The reviewer reports gradual improvement over the following months and says their son eventually regained the ability to walk, play, sleep and see without pain. They credit Dr. Ghalili's treatment with making the difference.

Both reviews are five stars. One reviewer had a two-year-old shoulder injury from a car accident and two rounds of physical therapy that did nothing, chose PRP, and reports improvement a month after the first treatment with a second already booked. The other came to discuss stem cell treatment for back pain and describes an evaluation that set out the options in plain terms.

This is a mobile IV service and the reviews reflect that. Two reviewers had drips delivered to their Las Vegas hotel rooms, name the nurses who came, James and Daniel, and report feeling more hydrated and more energetic afterwards. One notes add-ons were suggested without pressure. The third, a long-time customer, says the service changed after the company was sold in 2025, is no longer available around the clock, and quoted them a 16-hour wait.

All three reviews concern bio-identical hormone pellets. The two positive ones are around a decade old: long-term patients at the Chandler and Glendale offices who describe a clear physical and mental difference between appointments, and who name Steve Nunn and Dr. Rhodes. The most recent review is one star and describes repeated administrative errors, doctors changed without consent, and poor customer service.

Both reviewers give specific timelines. One, aged 81 and with fibromyalgia pain for close to 50 years, reports being pain free 14 weeks after the procedure and walking unaided after needing a walker. The other has had stem cell therapy for multiple sclerosis twice, and describes numbness below the waist receding within two months of the second round and their gait evening out by four months.

Two reviewers name Dr. Jaime Ewald, Dr. Lane and a staff member, Stan, and describe consultations they found honest and unhurried; one family drove from Reno for stem cell treatment for a father-in-law's traumatic brain injury. The third rates the clinic two stars: the staff were good, but they noticed no change after treatment and had no follow-up call or email.

All three reviews are five stars, and all describe a remote testosterone service rather than a clinic visit. One reviewer, 46 and with testosterone that had dropped sharply, reports better energy, focus and drive about two weeks into the program. The other two have been with the service longer and write about the practical side: quick scheduling, easy refills, shipments arriving on time, and providers who take questions without a sales push.

Both reviewers were treated by Dr. Brandt. One had stem cell treatment for a shoulder that made press-ups and swimming difficult, noticed a change within about two weeks, and says range of motion kept improving over the following six months. The other reports damaged spinal discs treated in both themselves and their wife, and frames the choice as an alternative to surgery.

All three reviewers had stem cell therapy at the Austin location and all wrote soon after the appointment, so they describe the visit rather than the result: staff named, including Kirsten and the nurse practitioner Selina, care taken over placing the injection, and how little it hurt. One adds that her husband had stem cells in his knee three years ago and has had no pain since.
